cells.tense: You are the one holding the scales right now, and your hands are steady.
cells.ask: Name one trade you keep letting run uneven and say what you'll do about it this week.
cells.core:
You can feel what's fair without doing arithmetic about it. Something in a split lands wrong and you notice it — not because you're keeping score, but because you're in contact with what's actually there. You give and receive in a way that keeps things moving between people. Others leave arrangements with you feeling even, and you didn't have to calculate a thing.

That steadiness is not a mood you happen to be in. It's working, and it's working quietly while you do other things. The clearing around you, the thing that just fell away — you're standing in it with your feet under you, which is why the adjustment is landing softly instead of like a correction. What this steadiness is free to feed next is the endings that are ready, the ones the moment is actually asking for.
cells.sheetLine: You feel what's fair, and you're steady enough to set it right.
cells.verb: Weighing what is fair and putting the scales back even
cells.place: In the sudden clearing where what couldn't hold has just fallen away

cells.tense: You are already living past the settlement, tallying a debt that has not been agreed to yet.
cells.ask: Pick one tally you've been running on someone and stop adding to it for three days.
cells.core:
You're running the accounts ahead of the moment. Every favor, every slight, every uneven thing gets a column, and somewhere in front of you is the version where it all comes out even. So you track instead of trade — what you hand over has become an entry and what comes back has become a claim. Watch what that does to the room: the people closest to you start to feel like counterparties.

The chance to hold something without needing it settled is right here, and it's the harder thing, not the softer one. You can carry a debt that hasn't been paid yet and still keep the relationship open. Holding that without forcing it is the practice; it will cost you the satisfaction of the tally.

cells.tense: You have been standing at a door that closed a long time ago, waiting for the terms to change.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're owed and ask for it plainly, in one sentence, without explaining why.
cells.core:
You know how to go without. When something is out of balance, you absorb the difference instead of naming it — and you've gotten good at it, good enough that it doesn't register as anything at all anymore. You don't ask people to settle with you; the asking is what stopped. So the exchange goes one way and you call it being easygoing.

That is what keeps the clearing from finishing its work. What's needed isn't a better sense of justice — it's the willingness to put one claim on the table and let it sit there. The practice here is small and solitary, not a confrontation: one sentence, one person, and then you let it stand. The refinement serves you, not a performance of fairness.
cells.sheetLine: You're owed something and you've stopped even asking for it.

cells.tense: You are keeping a tally right now that you would deny keeping if anyone asked.
cells.ask: Write down the one thing you keep resenting and haven't said, then read it once and put it away.
cells.core:
You've been weighing things without noticing you were doing it. A comment lands, a favor goes unreturned, and something in you records it — quietly, below the level where you'd call it anything. If someone asked whether you were keeping score, you'd say no, and you'd mean it. The counting is going; the saying-so isn't.

That is what's out of place. The fairness is already operating in you, accurate and wordless, and it keeps getting filed under 'nothing' or 'I'm fine.' The simpler thing to reach for is knowing what actually matters before you can argue for it. Notice the one thing you keep coming back to, name it to yourself, and let that be enough to start.
